text:
The three small circles have radius 2 and lie on the circle of radius \(11-2=9\) centred at \(O\).  
Let the centres be \(A,B,C\); then \(OA=OB=OC=9\).  

For a pair of circles, the chord of \(\Omega\) that is tangent to both and separates \(O\) from them is the external common tangent of the two equal circles.  
If the line through the centres \(AB\) is at a (unsigned) distance \(d_{AB}\) from \(O\), then the external tangent lies on the opposite side of \(AB\) and its distance from \(O\) is  

\[
p_{AB}=d_{AB}-2 .
\]

The chord length is \(L=2\sqrt{11^{2}-p^{2}}\).  
Two chords are given as \(4\sqrt{30}\); thus their distances from \(O\) satisfy  

\[
p= \sqrt{11^{2}-\Bigl(\tfrac{4\sqrt{30}}{2}\Bigr)^{2}}
   =\sqrt{121-120}=1 .
\]

Hence for the two corresponding sides of triangle \(ABC\),

\[
d_{AB}=p+2 = 3 .
\]

For any triangle inscribed in a circle of radius 9, the distance from the circum‑centre to a side equals \(9\cos\) of the opposite angle.  
Thus  

\[
9\cos A = 3,\qquad 9\cos B = 3,
\]
so \(\cos A=\cos B=\frac13\) and \(A=B\).  
Consequently  

\[
C=\pi-2A,\qquad
\cos C = -\cos(2A)=-(2\cos^{2}A-1)= -\bigl(2\cdot\frac19-1\bigr)=\frac79 .
\]

The third side of triangle \(ABC\) (the side opposite the third chord) therefore satisfies  

\[
9\cos C = d_{AC}=p_{AC}+2 \;\Longrightarrow\;
p_{AC}=9\cos C-2 = 7-2 =5 .
\]

Finally the length of the third chord is

\[
L_{3}=2\sqrt{11^{2}-5^{2}}
      =2\sqrt{121-25}
      =2\sqrt{96}
      =2\cdot4\sqrt6
      =8\sqrt6 .
\]

**Answer:**  
\(8\sqrt6\)
